headline: B-52反舰整合：签约在望，软件并网才是真门槛
lead: 美海军拟以独家来源方式与洛马签约，把隐身反舰导弹LRASM整合到B-52上。这一步若落地，将为轰炸机队补上专用反舰手段，但从软件并网、武器接口到安全分离验证的工程约束尚未走完，弹量与时间表仍无答案。

chapters.angle: 美海军拟以独家来源方式与洛马签约，把隐身反舰导弹LRASM整合到B-52上。这一步若落地，将为轰炸机队补上专用反舰手段，但从软件并网、武器接口到安全分离验证的工程约束尚未走完，弹量与时间表仍无答案。

sentences.text: 据一份10月7日的政府通告，美国海军正筹备与洛克希德·马丁公司签约，把隐身型AGM-158C远程反舰导弹整合到空军B-52轰炸机上。
海军航空系统司令部（NAVAIR）的通告称，该司令部打算与洛马进行独家来源谈判，随后授出一份成本加固定费用的交付订单，内容涵盖LRASM在B-52上的整合。

sentences.text: 从已披露的信息看，当前进展的实质是采购路径的确定，而非能力已经形成：独家来源谈判加成本加固定费用订单，说明美方认定洛马是唯一可行承包方，也说明项目仍处工程整合阶段。
这条路线的约束在于，把一种此前主要见于战斗机外挂使用的导弹接入轰炸机，需要改动的不只是挂架，还包括火控与任务软件，而这些改动在现有披露中仍属计划而非已完成事实。

sentences.text: 空军2027财年预算提案进一步列出计划，把LRASM和JASSM的最新改型整合到B-52上，其中包括尚未获准在该轰炸机上使用的版本。
2027财年的计划工作包括把导弹的作战飞行程序并入B-52基线轰炸机软件、验证从翼下挂点和内部挂载发射器分离武器的安全性、更新武器接口，并完成系统安全测试。

sentences.text: 这里有两条时间线：合同谈判与预算中的整合工程并行推进。若独家谈判顺利，落地节奏大概率受制于作战飞行程序并网和安全分离验证这类硬约束，而非签约本身——这两项在预算文件中被明确列为待完成工作。
成本与规模仍无从判断：通告未说明B-52最终会携带多少枚LRASM，因此单机打击容量和部队实际装备量都还不能下结论。

sentences.text: 与B-52现有的对陆打击手段相比，LRASM补上的是专用反舰能力；报道称，对B-52而言，加装LRASM将在其成熟的对面攻击武器库之外提供一种专用反舰武器。
尺寸上并非全新门槛：B-52最多可携带20枚JASSM，而LRASM与JASSM尺寸相同，理论上挂载兼容性有现成参照，但这只是尺寸层面的可比性，不等于整合已获验证。
海上作战也非首次：B-52还通过Quickstrike系列航空水雷展示了布雷能力，反舰导弹与之构成不同层次的海上拒止手段。

sentences.text: 判断：短期内这是一次采购路径的推进，而非战备状态的跃升；真正决定成败的是软件并网与安全分离验证能否按期完成。
值得观察的四点：独家来源谈判是否转为正式交付订单；B-52基线软件是否纳入LRASM作战飞行程序；翼下挂点与内部发射器的安全分离验证是否通过；以及预算中尚未获批的LRASM改型是否获得B-52使用许可。
另可留意后续是否披露单机携带量与部署方向，现有信息尚不支持对印太部署规模作具体判断。

events.title: B-52 To Get Stealthy AGM-158C Long-Range Anti-Ship Missiles
events.originalTitle: B-52 To Get Stealthy AGM-158C Long-Range Anti-Ship Missiles
events.excerpt: The U.S. Navy is preparing to sign a contract with Lockheed Martin to integrate the stealthy AGM-158C Long Range Anti-Ship Missile (LRASM) onto the Air Force’s B-52 Stratofortress bombers, according to an October 7 government notice. The effort would add another long-range maritime strike option to the U.S. bomber force as the military looks to counter increasingly capable adversary naval forces, especially in the Indo-Pacific theater. Joint Air-to-Surface Standoff Missiles are prepared to be loaded onto a U.S. Air Force B-52 on Andersen Air Force Base, Guam, on April 24, 2023.

evidenceRecords.text: The U.S. Navy is preparing to sign a contract with Lockheed Martin to integrate the stealthy AGM-158C Long Range Anti-Ship Missile (LRASM) onto the Air Force’s B-52 Stratofortress bombers, according to an October 7 government notice.

The effort would add another long-range maritime strike option to the U.S. bomber force as the military looks to counter increasingly capable adversary naval forces, especially in the Indo-Pacific theater.

U.S. Willis The latest Naval Air Systems Command (NAVAIR) notice says the command intends to enter into sole-source negotiations with Lockheed Martin and subsequently award a cost-plus-fixed-fee delivery order covering LRASM integration on the B-52.
The B-52 can carry up to 20 JASSMs, and the weapons have the same dimensions, but the government notice does not specify how many LRASMs the bomber would ultimately carry.
A B-52 flies across the Atlantic Ocean on June 17, 2019, for a flight in support of Exercise BALTOPS 2019, the largest multinational maritime exercise of the year in the Baltic Sea.

The U.S. Air Force’s Fiscal Year 2027 budget proposal further outlines plans to integrate the latest variants of LRASM and JASSM onto the B-52, including versions not yet cleared for use on the bomber.

Planned work in FY2027 includes incorporating the missiles’ operational flight programs into the B-52’s baseline bomber software, validating safe weapon separation from both wing-mounted stations and the internal carriage launcher, updating armament interfaces, and completing system-safety testing.
Joint Air-to-Surface Standoff Missiles are prepared to be loaded onto a U.S. Air Force B-52 on Andersen Air Force Base, Guam, on April 24, 2023.
An AGM-158C Long Range Anti-Ship Missile is seen under the wing of an F/A-18, with another missile in the foreground.
U.S. Navy For the B-52, the addition of LRASM would provide a dedicated anti-ship weapon alongside its established land-attack arsenal.
The B-52 also has a demonstrated naval mine-laying capability through the Quickstrike family of aerial mines.

history.title: Extreme Environments Push Chips To Their Breaking Point
history.originalTitle: Extreme Environments Push Chips To Their Breaking Point

evidenceRecords.text: Key Takeaways: Orbital data centers, military/aerospace vehicles, HPC experiments, quantum, and advanced manufacturing equipment are all putting pressure on chips to withstand extreme environments.
Chips that were once qualified against a limited set of operating conditions are now being designed for environments where multiple stresses hit at once.

For example, Pacific Northwest National Laboratory (PNNL) is working with Morgan State University, Northrop Grumman, and Project Omega on the DARPA-funded Rads to Watts program, which aims to convert Cold War-era radioactive decay into high-density nuclear micro-power radiovoltaic systems for extreme environments, including space, remote sensing, undersea infrastructure, and defense applications. [1] Radioisotopes such as Strontium-90 will be converted directly into electricity to operate for decades without refueling or battery replacement.

history.title: Energy Department Announces New Genesis Mission Awards to Accelerate Scientific Capability
history.originalTitle: Energy Department Announces New Genesis Mission Awards to Accelerate Scientific Capability

evidenceRecords.text: Insider Brief The Department of Energy announced $159 million for 12 new Phase II Genesis Mission projects using AI and advanced computing to accelerate scientific research.
The projects include Harvard -led quantum computing error correction, Oak Ridge-led quantum magnet design, and efforts in fusion energy, biotechnology, geothermal energy and particle physics.

PRESS RELEASE — The U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) today announced 12 Phase II project awards for President Trump’s historic Genesis Mission, totaling $159 million, that will expand efforts to harness artificial intelligence (AI), advanced computing, and the nation’s world-class scientific capabilities to accelerate the pace of discovery.

By connecting America’s leading scientists with advanced AI, supercomputing, scientific data and DOE’s unique research infrastructure, the Genesis Mission is creating new capabilities to accelerate scientific discovery and expand the frontiers of U.S. science and technology.
The Department of Energy announced $159 million for 12 new Phase II Genesis Mission projects using AI and advanced computing to accelerate scientific research.
The projects include Harvard-led quantum computing error correction, Oak Ridge-led quantum magnet design, and efforts in fusion energy, biotechnology, geothermal energy and particle physics.
The awards build on the Genesis Mission’s growing portfolio of projects, first announced in July, to address critical national science and technology challenges.

In 2023, fabrication of NV centers was demonstrated at production scale under Germany’s national quantum computing initiative – the “transistor” manufactured repeatably rather than hand-assembled one defect at a time.

That figure deserves attention because almost no competing spin-defect platform has published a fabrication yield at all, and yield is the industrial question – how reliably usable qubits can be placed where they are wanted, at scale.
The first is a transistor moment.
In 2020, researchers in Leipzig, Germany, demonstrated the first working one-qubit diamond-based quantum computer – proof that the device physics worked outside a research setting.
Diamond – The Silicon of Quantum Computing?
Whether NV-center diamond is quantum computing’s silicon – the material system that wins the platform war – is an open question.
Silicon-vacancy and tin-vacancy centers in diamond have so far worked only at cryogenic temperatures, and other spin centers could eventually prove better.
